analysis.investment_thesis: Super Iron Foundry is a tiny (INR 66 Cr mcap) castings exporter with a weak return profile (ROE 6.2%, ROCE 7.4%) trading at 25x earnings — the story simply doesn't add up for GARP. With no disclosed growth rate to justify the P/E, the implied PEG is well above my 1.0 threshold.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 70.88% signals skin in the game
Established since 1988 with export exposure in castings
Micro-cap size leaves theoretical room to grow if execution improves
key_risks: ROE 6.2% is below cost of capital — value destruction, not creation
P/E of 25.4x is unjustified without visible 20%+ earnings growth (PEG likely >2)
Cyclical castings/forgings industry with commodity-like margins and FX risk
red_flags: P/E (25.4) far exceeds ROE (6.2%) — classic overvalued slow grower
Sub-8% ROCE in a capital-intensive foundry business
No growth narrative disclosed to support multiple
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is a classic "slow grower dressed up as a fast grower" setup that I warn about. A foundry earning only 6.2% on equity and 7.4% on capital employed is barely covering its cost of capital, yet the market is pricing it at 25x earnings. For that multiple to make sense, earnings would need to compound at 20%+ annually — and nothing in castings & forgings, a cyclical commodity-adjacent business, suggests that trajectory. The PEG math doesn't work.

At INR 66 Cr market cap, Super Iron is small enough to be a ten-bagger in theory, but Lynch's rule is "growth at a reasonable price," not "small at any price." I'd want to see ROE climbing toward 15%+, export order book acceleration, and a P/E closer to 10-12x before getting interested. Until the returns-on-capital story inflects, this is a pass — I'd rather hunt in the same industrials sector for a foundry compounding earnings 20%+ at a PEG under 0.8.
